lead: Alexandria plumbing deals with some of the oldest homes in the country, river flooding and cold snaps. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Alexandria.
risk: old galvanized and cast-iron pipes, basement and tidal flooding and frozen pipes
risk_short: old pipes, flooding and frozen pipes
why: Old Town has row houses from the 1700s and 1800s, and Del Ray and Rosemont have homes from the early 1900s. Many have galvanized supply lines, cast-iron stacks and old sewer laterals.
Low parts of Old Town flood from the Potomac and heavy rain. Older parts of the city have combined sewers, which the RiverRenew tunnel project is fixing.
water: Alexandria's water comes from Virginia American Water, which buys treated Potomac River water from Fairfax Water. It is moderately hard.
tips: Check historic district rules before exterior work.
Consider a backwater valve if your basement has flooded.
Scope the sewer lateral before buying.
areas: PipeMend works in Old Town, Del Ray, Rosemont, Seminary Hill, Arlandria, Parkfairfax, Carlyle, the West End and every other Alexandria neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Alexandria Department of Code Administration, and plumbers must hold a tradesman license from the Virginia Board for Contractors (DPOR).

faq.q: Are there special rules for plumbing in Old Town Alexandria?
faq.a: Work that changes the outside of a historic building may need approval from the city's historic review boards. Interior plumbing usually needs only a regular permit.
